raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- `--engram-config` `lookup` gains `auto` (the new default), `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter` and `all_to_all`, next to `peer_read`; `collective`, the old default, is still accepted as `auto`.
- Under DP attention, every rank needs rows for its own tokens while each Engram table is split across the TP group. For eager prefill (SUM_LEN) batches on CUDA with one DP rank per TP rank, the lookup now gathers the hash ids with `all_gatherv` and then:
  - `all_to_all`: each rank looks up only the hash columns it holds, for every rank's tokens, and sends each rank its part; it moves 1/tp of the bytes the reductions move. It needs the 24 hash columns to divide over the TP group.
  - `reduce_scatter`: the zero-filled lookup summed with a variable-length reduce-scatter.
- `auto` picks `all_to_all` whenever the columns divide. Decode (MAX_LEN) batches, CUDA-graph captures, prefill CP, ROCm and layouts the columns do not divide over keep their current collective, as does `all_reduce`. The choice no longer depends on `SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV`.
- An explicit `reduce_scatter` or `all_to_all` is rejected at startup without DP attention on CUDA, and `all_to_all` when the columns do not divide over `--tp-size`.
- Docs: the Engram tables page explains the choices and how `auto` picks; the server argument row lists the values.

No behavior change outside eager prefill lookups under DP attention on CUDA; those return the same rows, bit for bit.

Related: #46338 (reduce-scatter for uniform prefill batches of 32K rows or more per rank).

## Microbenchmark

One DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Engram layer at its real size (24 hash columns, 256-wide rows) as a host `per_rank` table, each rank bound to its GPU's NUMA node; the full DP lookup (gather the ids, look up the rows, exchange them), eager, slowest rank's median per layer. Every `all_to_all` result was checked bit for bit against `reduce_scatter`, in all 144 shapes.

Uniform tokens per rank:

| GPU | DP | Tokens per rank | `all_reduce` (us) | `reduce_scatter` (us) | `all_to_all` (us) | `all_to_all` vs `all_reduce` (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB300 | 2 | 2,048 | 436 | 250 | 272 | -38 |
| GB300 | 2 | 8,192 | 976 | 694 | 738 | -24 |
| GB300 | 2 | 32,768 | 3,214 | 2,480 | 2,607 | -19 |
| GB300 | 4 | 2,048 | 560 | 359 | 272 | -51 |
| GB300 | 4 | 8,192 | 1,579 | 1,019 | 763 | -52 |
| GB300 | 4 | 32,768 | 5,627 | 3,613 | 2,690 | -52 |
| B300 | 2 | 2,048 | 1,107 | 1,051 | 1,008 | -9 |
| B300 | 2 | 8,192 | 3,581 | 3,400 | 3,307 | -8 |
| B300 | 2 | 32,768 | 9,981 | 9,322 | 8,996 | -10 |
| B300 | 4 | 2,048 | 1,433 | 1,323 | 793 | -45 |
| B300 | 4 | 8,192 | 3,949 | 3,461 | 2,855 | -28 |
| B300 | 4 | 32,768 | 11,227 | 9,267 | 7,026 | -37 |
| B300 | 8 | 2,048 | 1,669 | 1,485 | 700 | -58 |
| B300 | 8 | 8,192 | 5,026 | 4,169 | 2,465 | -51 |
| B300 | 8 | 32,768 | 15,809 | 12,955 | 6,491 | -59 |
| H200 | 2 | 2,048 | 2,259 | 2,141 | 1,473 | -35 |
| H200 | 2 | 8,192 | 5,608 | 5,193 | 5,065 | -10 |
| H200 | 2 | 32,768 | 15,330 | 13,839 | 13,263 | -13 |
| H200 | 4 | 2,048 | 2,128 | 1,903 | 1,177 | -45 |
| H200 | 4 | 8,192 | 6,218 | 5,321 | 4,399 | -29 |
| H200 | 4 | 32,768 | 17,699 | 14,150 | 10,553 | -40 |
| H200 | 8 | 2,048 | 2,368 | 2,113 | 1,030 | -57 |
| H200 | 8 | 8,192 | 7,233 | 6,207 | 3,589 | -50 |
| H200 | 8 | 32,768 | 24,564 | 20,376 | 10,282 | -58 |

Fastest choice over 18 shapes per row: 512 to 65,536 tokens per rank, uniform or skewed (halving per rank, or one rank at 1/8):

| GPU | DP | Fastest: `all_to_all` | Fastest: `reduce_scatter` | Fastest: `all_reduce` | `all_to_all` slower than `all_reduce` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB300 | 2 | 1 of 18 | 17 | 0 | 0 |
| GB300 | 4 | 15 of 18 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| B300 | 2 | 15 of 18 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| B300 | 4 | 18 of 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B300 | 8 | 18 of 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| H200 | 2 | 18 of 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| H200 | 4 | 18 of 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| H200 | 8 | 18 of 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

`all_to_all` is the fastest choice almost everywhere and never slower than `all_reduce` by more than 8 us. On GB300 at DP 2, `reduce_scatter` is about 5% ahead at large batches: `all_to_all` then spends ~440 us at 32K tokens per rank reordering the received rows from [source rank, token] to [token], a copy that can later fold into the quantization before `wkv`.

## Checks

- The `EngramEmbedding` DP lookup itself on GB300, DP 2 and 4, host `per_rank`, randomly filled rows: `reduce_scatter`, `all_to_all` and `auto` match `all_reduce` bit for bit with uniform, skewed, one empty rank, and 3-6 tokens per rank. At 32K tokens per rank, DP 4: `all_reduce` 5,860 us per layer, `auto` 2,765 us.
- Serving on GB300, DP 2 with MegaMoE, host `per_rank` tables and DSpark, 16K-token prompts with 1 output token at concurrency 64: input throughput 141,733 and 144,409 tok/s with `all_reduce`, 143,798 / 140,759 / 142,753 / 143,391 tok/s with `auto`, within run-to-run spread (the change saves about 0.5 ms of a ~115 ms step at 8K tokens per rank).

 |---|---|---|
 | `placement` | Where do the rows live? | `gpu` (default): device memory. `cpu`: pinned host memory, which the GPU reads in place; the HBM goes to the KV cache. |
 | `replication` | How many copies are there? | `none` (default): one table, its rows split across the TP group. `per_node`: each node holds the whole table, mapped by all of its ranks. |
-| `lookup` | How does a rank get rows another rank holds? Only with `replication` `none`. | `collective` (default): every rank looks up the rows it holds for all tokens, and a reduction assembles them. `peer_read`: each rank reads its tokens' rows straight from the owning GPU's shard, with no collective. |
+| `lookup` | How does a rank get rows another rank holds? Only with `replication` `none`. | `auto` (default): a collective SGLang picks for each step. `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter`, `all_to_all`: that collective (see below). `peer_read`: each rank reads its tokens' rows straight from the owning GPU's shard over NVLink, with no collective. |
 
 The resolved configuration is logged at startup as `DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables: ...`.
 
@@ -47,6 +47,31 @@ sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 8 --attn-dp-
   runs per step, a cost that grows with the group size.
 - **Latency-bound serving with memory to spare**: the default keeps every lookup in device memory.
 
+## How `auto` picks the collective
+
+Under DP attention, every rank needs rows for its own tokens, but each table is split across the
+TP group. The lookup gathers every rank's hash ids, looks up rows, and exchanges them:
+
+- `all_reduce`: every rank looks up the rows it holds for all tokens, zero for the rest, and an
+  all-reduce sums the buffers; each rank keeps its own slice.
+- `reduce_scatter`: the same lookup, summed with a reduce-scatter that hands each rank only its own
+  tokens' rows.
+- `all_to_all`: each rank looks up only the hash columns it holds, for all tokens, and sends each
+  rank its part. It moves `1 / tp_size` of the bytes the other two move, and needs the 24 hash
+  columns to divide over the TP group (DP 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12).
+
+On CUDA, with one DP rank per TP rank and no context parallelism, `auto` uses `all_to_all` for
+eager prefill batches whenever the columns divide, and elsewhere keeps the collective it used
+before (a reduce-scatter for decode batches, an all-reduce otherwise). Measured on GB300, B300 and
+H200 at DP 2-8 with host tables, from 512 to 65,536 tokens per rank, `all_to_all` was the fastest
+in 121 of 144 shapes and never more than 8 us slower than the all-reduce; at 8,192 tokens per rank and
+up it was 6-60% faster. The exception is GB300 at DP 2, where `reduce_scatter` is faster. Every
+choice returns the same rows.
+
+An explicit `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter` or `all_to_all` applies to the same eager prefill
+lookups; decode batches and CUDA-graph replays keep their collective, and without DP attention the
+lookup is always an all-reduce.
+
 ## Requirements and limits
 
 - **`placement` `cpu`**: host RAM for the whole table across the node's ranks, and a longer load.

 - **`replication` `per_node`**: one shared memory file per TP group, which the other ranks open
   through `/proc`. The TP group must sit on one node (`--nnodes 1`) and the ranks must share a PID
   namespace. This mapping usually gets no huge pages unless shmem transparent huge pages are on.
+- **`lookup` `reduce_scatter` or `all_to_all`**: DP attention on CUDA; `all_to_all` also needs the
+  hash columns to divide over `--tp-size`.
 - **`lookup` `peer_read`**: CUDA with peer access between the GPUs (POSIX handles within a node,
   fabric handles across an NVLink domain). Each GPU holds `1 / tp_size` of the table. With TP1
   there is no peer, and the setting has no effect.

+        exchange = self._dp_exchange(sizes)
+        if exchange is None:
+            return self._dp_global_buffer_lookup(indices, forward_batch)
+        if sum(sizes) == 0:
+            return self.new_rows(indices)
+        group = get_parallel().tp_group
+        ids = indices.new_empty((sum(sizes), *indices.shape[1:]))
+        group.all_gatherv(indices.contiguous(), sizes=sizes, output=ids)
+        if exchange == EngramLookup.REDUCE_SCATTER:
+            values = self._owned_rows(ids).view(ids.shape[0], -1)

+        k, n = self._cols_per_rank, indices.shape[0]

+            recv.view(self.tp_size, n, k, self.dim)
+            .transpose(0, 1)

+    def _dp_exchange(self, sizes: Optional[list[int]]) -> Optional[str]:

+        if sizes is None or self.lookup == EngramLookup.ALL_REDUCE:
+            return None
+        if self.lookup == EngramLookup.REDUCE_SCATTER:
+            return EngramLookup.REDUCE_SCATTER
+        # Measured fastest at DP 2-8 on GB300, B300 and H200, except GB300 at DP 2.
+        return EngramLookup.ALL_TO_ALL if self._cols_per_rank is not None else None
+
+    def _eager_dp_sizes(
+        self, indices: torch.Tensor, forward_batch: ForwardBatch
+    ) -> Optional[list[int]]:
+        """Per-rank token counts if the lookup may exchange only the real rows, else None."""
+        parallel = get_parallel()
+        padding = forward_batch.dp_padding_mode
+        if (
+            _is_hip
+            or padding is None
+            or padding.is_max_len()
+            or parallel.attn_cp_size > 1
+            or self.tp_size != parallel.attn_dp_size
+            or world_dp_gather_enabled()
+            or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+        ):
+            return None
+        sizes = get_dp_global_num_tokens()
+        if (
+            sizes is None
+            or len(sizes) != self.tp_size
+            or sizes[parallel.attn_dp_rank] != indices.shape[0]
+        ):
+            return None
+        return list(sizes)
+
+    def _dp_global_buffer_lookup(
+        self, indices: torch.Tensor, forward_batch: ForwardBatch
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Look up every DP rank's indices in the global DP buffer and reduce them."""
